newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Spectrum values reserves at over US$400m.
newsitem.headline: Spectrum values reserves at over US$400m.

text.p: Spectrum Resources on Thursday estimated its proven and indicated reserves of nickel and copper had a value of over US$400 (NZ$620) million.
The revised reserves figures in the mineral explorer's quarterly report follow two drilling programmes so far this year at Ban Phuc in Vietnam.
The results of the drilling have converted some indicated reserves in the upper levels of a massive sulphide zone into proven reserves and located extensions to known resources.

The drilling programmes have also investigated and converted some inferred nickel resources into indicated reserves and verified the accuracy of analysis from Vietnamese drilling carried out from 1960 to 1962, the company said.

Manual calculation of new reserve figures for the two types of mineralisation at Ban Phuc show the massive sulphide zone holds 1.78 million tonnes of ore containing an average 2.1 percent nickel and 1 percent copper, the company said.
"Although the significant increase in tonnage obtained is at a lower grade, the original higher grade smaller reserve in included in the new figure."
In the zone of cumulate sulphide the indicated reserves were 1.47 million tonnes containing 1.2 percent nickel.
Regional exploration during the latest three months has located previously unknown structures which are being evaluated for nickel content.

"Small pockets of high grade nickel and copper sulphide mineralisation were located in a major shear zone east of the Ban Mong prospect thus increasing the prospectivity of this target area," the report said.
Spectrum plans further drilling at Ban Phuc over the next six months to define more cumulate sulphide resources.
Exploration activity during the quarter was concentrated in Vietnam with no significant work done in Chile or New Zealand, the company said.
New Zealand-listed Spectrum achieved a listing on the Vancouver Stock Exchange in May.
